segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive
within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or
(f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'Motor vehicle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate' and is claimed with the admitted id, never expanded into classes, as the index maps 'The driver of a motor vehicle' for NRS_484B_270_1. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is no aggregate: ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency) and the atom reads the vehicle's class only.

Reuses the index mapping of 'shall yield' (kin.speed, rel.contact). To yield is to give the other precedence: what the subject does is its motion, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity', read to tell a moving subject from one at rest; a failure that ends in a crash is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'. rel.contact is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss': the near miss is bounded by the operationalization of t3, not by this atom.

'Riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device; the ontology reads who controls a road user's motion through that motion, so the person riding is the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance, as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1 (observable_reading, agency). kin.speed carries no exclusion that applies.

'Bicycle', 'electric bicycle' and 'electric scooter' are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter); ru.aggregate is claimed with each admitted id, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter' for NRS_484B_270_2a_o1, and never replaced by ru.bicycle, ru.electric_bicycle or ru.electric_scooter.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); claimed as ru.aggregate with that id, as the index maps 'A pedestrian' for NRS_484B_297_6_o1.

'the pathway or lane' is the pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters the line names: st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'. The other road user is on it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane to that road user so the rule reads its own lane l and not any lane of the scene; the obligation reads the same l again for the subject. Neither contract states an exclusion that applies.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle (ru.aggregate), read as driven through its controlled motion.
obligation: For every road user p of the scene other than the subject, and every bicycle lane or path l (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) whose region p's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) at the observation, where p is either (i) a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, or (ii) a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian to whom NRS_484B_297_6_o1 applies (ruleApplies, its subject mapped to p): the subject's body is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject's footprint overlaps that same l while the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance and prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Read at every observation; an unobserved occupancy, contact or closest approach leaves the verdict unknown where it decides it.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion: who or what is at the controls is not observed, and the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.
'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance: a rider halted in the lane is not read as riding.

The yield is read on the lane the other occupies: the subject fails to yield where it touches the other, or where its footprint overlaps that lane while it moves with a conflicting closest approach to the other; a conflict while the subject stays outside that lane is not read as a failure to yield on the pathway or lane.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car (member of the motor vehicle aggregate) turning right moves across a bicycle lane; its footprint overlaps the lane while a moving bicycle in that lane closes from behind, their closest approach falling within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts short of the bicycle lane until the moving bicycle has gone by, then crosses the lane; while it overlaps the lane there is no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any rider in it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a bicycle (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) riding in the bicycle lane behind another bicycle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car's footprint is near the bicycle lane while a moving electric scooter closes on it with a conflicting closest approach; the source does not observe footprint occupancy, so whether the scooter is on the lane and whether the car overlaps it are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car crosses the bicycle lane into a driveway; no bicycle, electric bicycle, electric scooter or pedestrian is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks in the bicycle lane while the sidewalk beside it is clear and unobstructed, so NRS_484B_297_6_o1 does not apply to it; the car enters the lane with a conflicting closest approach to the pedestrian but no contact.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_2, except that the pedestrian has stepped from the sidewalk into the bicycle lane to move around an obstruction on the sidewalk, so NRS_484B_297_6_o1 applies to it.

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
or a pedestrian
as provided in subsection 6 of NRS 484B.297 [NRS-484B-297-6]
on the pathway or lane.
The driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter, stop, stand, park or drive
within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
except: (a) When entering or exiting an alley or driveway;
(b) When operating or parking a disabled vehicle;
(c) To avoid conflict with other traffic;
(d) In the performance of official duties;
(e) In compliance with the directions of a police officer;
or
(f) In an emergency.

elements.justification: 'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is claimed with the admitted id. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, not membership (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'): it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

Every verb is a way of having the vehicle's footprint in the lane: to enter is its footprint coming to overlap the lane, to drive within it is to overlap it while moving, and to stop, stand or park is to overlap it while halted. 'Stop' here is prohibited, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'); 'stand' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle') and 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle') are halts too. Moving and halted together are every observation of the footprint in the lane, so the prohibition is read on rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', of a st.bicycle_lane_or_path region, whatever the motion; no exclusion of either contract applies. The exceptions of DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer') coincide with exceptions (c) and (e) and are carried there.

'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... bicycle lane ...)', which anchors the lane l to the subject. 'Provided' is the status of a feature, read through the lane's presence (observable_reading, status).

'Alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015, 'a highway: (1) Within a city block set apart for public use ... (2) Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'driveway' (DEF-NRS-484A-190, 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel') meets the highway at st.driveway_or_alley_entrance, 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'. That atom is 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there', a distinction the exception does not need, since it covers alley and driveway alike. Entering or exiting is read through the subject's footprint (rel.occupies): its stretch in the lane l runs until its footprint overlaps such a region (entering), or has run since an observation at which it overlapped one (exiting).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is 'both indicators flashing together', a signal, not the vehicle's condition; kin.engine_running is 'propulsion is available', 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt'. Neither denotes a disabled vehicle, and the condition of a road user is never an assumption.

'Traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'). The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap the lane (rel.occupies rising), a member of traffic other than the subject was in conflict with it, prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. The primitives are 'Not a stand-in for: contact between bodies, the clearance between bodies, or the danger of a crash ... alone': they bound a traffic conflict under the conflict convention, which is what the words name, not a contact.

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): ru.emergency_vehicle ('vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency', 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle') and ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment') state what the vehicle is, never what it is doing; sig.warning_lamp ('a warning lamp lit') is shown by vehicles on duty and off it alike, and many official duties (a patrol, an inspection, a delivery of mail) show none. No conduct or feature the ontology carries tells a vehicle performing official duties from one that is not.

'Police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180, 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') directing traffic is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}', with role police_officer; the direction reaches the subject where it governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region, the abstract union of the kinds dev.governs admits, among them the bicycle lane or path) whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), as the index maps 'or the directions of a police officer'. dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position': it is read as control of the region, not as where the subject must halt. The officer's authority is read through the direction's presence (observable_reading, status).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap below): sig.hazard is a signal, not a peril; ru.emergency_vehicle is a class and 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'. Neither denotes an emergency, which is never an assumption.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven, and its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a bicycle lane or path l (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) at the observation.
obligation: At that observation one of the exceptions holds for the same l: (a) the subject's footprint overlaps l at every observation until one at which it overlaps an alley (st.alley) or a driveway or alley entrance (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance) (until), or has overlapped l at every observation since one at which it overlapped such a region (since); (b) [gap: a disabled vehicle]; (c) at the observation at which the subject's footprint came to overlap l (the latest rise of its overlap, read with since), some road user u other than the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, had prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; (d) [gap: the vehicle in the performance of official duties]; (e) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a travel region whose region the subject's footprint overlaps; (f) [gap: an emergency]. Where none holds, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'provided' for bicycles is the lane's legal status, read through the presence of the mapped bicycle lane or path.
The purpose 'to avoid conflict' is read through the conduct it explains: a conflict with other traffic at the moment the subject came into the lane.
The officer's authority is read through the presence of a person directing traffic in the police_officer role.
Entering, stopping, standing, parking and driving within the lane are read together as any overlap of the subject's footprint with the lane, since together they cover every motion state.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along a bicycle lane for a block; its stretch in the lane neither begins at nor ends in an alley or driveway entrance, no traffic was in conflict with it when it came into the lane, it is neither an emergency nor an official vehicle, and no officer directs traffic there.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car crosses the bicycle lane; its footprint overlaps the lane at every observation until it overlaps a driveway entrance it turns into.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives in the travel lane next to the bicycle lane; its footprint never overlaps the bicycle lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along the edge of a bicycle lane with no exception present; the source does not observe footprint occupancy, so whether the car is within the lane is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A police officer directing traffic governs the bicycle lane and the car drives within it at the officer's direction.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car swerves into the bicycle lane at an observation at which another car merging into its lane has a conflicting closest approach with it, and stays in the lane until it has passed.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A utility crew's marked vehicle stands in the bicycle lane while the crew repairs a signal, in the performance of official duties.

gaps.proposal: ru.on_official_duty | the road user is being used, at the observation, in the performance of the duties of a public office or of a contracted public service (an enforcement action, a repair of the road or its devices, a public inspection), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** the vehicle's class or livery, or its warning lamps — an official vehicle may be off duty and a vehicle on duty may show no lamp | general
gaps.nearest: ru.emergency_vehicle and ru.official_vehicle (classes: what a vehicle is, not what it is doing); sig.warning_lamp (a lamp lit, shown on and off duty alike). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may enter, stand in or move through a bicycle lane, which only the duty being performed decides.

gaps.proposal: ru.disabled | a vehicle that cannot move under its own power or cannot be driven on (a breakdown, crash damage, a flat tyre), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a halt, a set parking brake or lit hazard lamps — a vehicle at rest with its hazards lit may be fully operable | general
gaps.nearest: sig.hazard (both indicators flashing together: a signal a driver chooses to emit, not the vehicle's condition); kin.engine_running (propulsion available; 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt', and a disabled vehicle may still run its engine). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may stand in or move through a bicycle lane, which the vehicle's condition, not its signals, decides.

gaps.proposal: env.emergency | a sudden peril at the observation that a road user's conduct answers to (a fire, a medical emergency, a crash or a hazard ahead), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** an emergency vehicle's class, its lamps or its siren | general
gaps.nearest: sig.hazard (a signal, not a peril); ru.emergency_vehicle (a class; 'Not a stand-in for: a responding emergency vehicle'). The exception decides whether a motor vehicle may enter or stand in a bicycle lane, which only the existence of the emergency decides.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3 [NRS-484B-270-3],
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall not enter or proceed through an intersection
while driving within a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'the driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_2a_o1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), since ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.

'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another'; '(3) The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', whose exclusion of the alley junction is the definition's own. It is 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line': the words name the intersection itself. Entering it and proceeding through it are the subject's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies) while moving.

'a pathway or lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; 'within' it is rel.occupies, which anchors that lane to the subject. 'Driving' is the vehicle's controlled motion, read as kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading, agency). No exclusion of these contracts applies.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a bicycle lane or path (st.bicycle_lane_or_path) at the observation.
obligation: At that observation the subject's footprint overlaps no intersection (st.intersection), or NRS_484B_270_3_o2 is complied with by the subject at that observation (rule, subject mapped to subject): what subsection 3 otherwise provides is its exceptions, under which the subject may drive within the lane, through the intersection included. Where the subject overlaps an intersection and that rule is violated, the duty is violated; where either is unknown and the other does not decide, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'driving within' is read as the vehicle moving above the halt tolerance with its footprint overlapping the lane.
Entering and proceeding through an intersection are read at every observation at which the moving subject's footprint overlaps both the bicycle lane or path and an intersection.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along a bicycle lane and enters an intersection from it; no exception of subsection 3 holds (no alley or driveway, no conflict at its entry into the lane, not an emergency or official vehicle, no officer directing).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A police officer directing traffic governs the bicycle lane; at the officer's direction a car drives within the lane and proceeds through the intersection, complying with NRS_484B_270_3_o2 under its exception (e).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car in the general travel lane enters the intersection; its footprint never overlaps the bicycle lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along the edge of a bicycle lane into an intersection with no exception present; footprint occupancy is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car drives within the bicycle lane and turns into a driveway before reaching the intersection; its footprint never overlaps an intersection.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision
with a person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'The driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of w2 bounds separately.

'a person riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device, read as the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading, agency), as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1.

Reuses the index mapping of 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.' (NRS_484B_270_1): the three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, never expanded into class atoms.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the rider, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user b other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter and moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance: the subject is not in contact with b (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance; a rider at rest is not read.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a riding bicyclist or scooter rider; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A moving car closes on a bicycle riding ahead in the same lane; their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance and the car does not slow.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car slows behind the moving bicycle and keeps a closest approach beyond p.conflict_centre_clearance, then passes with a wide berth; no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is an electric scooter (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) riding near a bicycle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A moving car passes alongside a riding electric bicycle with no conflicting closest approach; contact between bodies is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moving car drives on an empty street: no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Intentionally
interfere with the movement
of a motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate, as the index maps 'any motor vehicle'.

The movement of the motor vehicle is its motion: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the vehicle moving, above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed', whose braking shows the movement disturbed; it is 'Not a stand-in for: speed', and it is read here as the change the interference forces, not as the speed. The rider interferes from in front of the vehicle's movement: rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', with the rider's bearing in the vehicle's frame pointing ahead. No exclusion applies.

operationalizations.standard: intentionally interfere (intent, a state of mind, and the degree of interference)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: an interference with a vehicle's movement is a conflict in which the vehicle, with the rider ahead of it, brakes evasively — a deceleration beyond comfortable service braking while their closest approach lies within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
obligation: At every observation, for every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), it is not the case that: the subject lies ahead of m (the longitudinal component of the subject's rel.bearing in m's frame is positive), m's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below the negative of p.vehicle_evasive_decel, and prim.closest_approach_within(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.

Intent shows in no single observation: it is read only through the conduct that interferes — the rider ahead of a moving motor vehicle in a conflict that forces it to brake evasively — and a conflict the rider did not seek is not told apart; an interference that forces no evasive braking (a swerve only) is not read.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Overtake and pass a motor vehicle
unless the operator can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Overtake and pass' is drv.interaction.overtake_pass, whose contract is 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with a the subject and b the motor vehicle, as the index maps 'approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle'; it 'says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves', so a pass of a moving or a standing motor vehicle is covered alike. 'A motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate.

operationalizations.standard: safely, without endangering the operator or the occupants of the motor vehicle
operationalizations.convention: bicyclist operating space: a pass is safe where the gap between the rider's body and the passed vehicle's body stays at least the rider's operating-space sway and the bodies never touch; traffic-conflict technique: no other road user comes into a closest approach within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance during the pass

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
obligation: For every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle: at each observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, m) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos holds (the pass's recognition), the pass was safe at every observation since its beginning — the last observation of the window behind at which m was ahead of the subject (positive longitudinal component of m's rel.bearing in the subject's frame, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with headings aligned within p.overtake_same_direction_cos (rel.same_direction), read with since: at each such observation the subject is not in contact with m (rel.contact), its rel.surface_gap to m is at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap, and no road user u other than the subject and m has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where the pass is recognized and the pass was not safe throughout, violated; an unobserved gap, contact or closest approach that decides it leaves it unknown.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.
'can do so safely' is the operator's judgement of the pass, read through the pass actually made: its clearance and the conflicts during it.

Endangering the occupants of the motor vehicle is read through the clearance to and contact with its body, which carries them; endangering the operator is read through that clearance and through conflicting closest approaches with every other road user during the pass; other hazards (the surface, the operator's speed) are not read.

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision
with a pedestrian.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of x2 bounds separately.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate as the index maps 'A pedestrian'.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the pedestrian, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a pedestrian; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise
proper caution
upon observing
a pedestrian:
(1) On or near a highway, street or road;
(2) At or near a bus stop or bench, shelter or transit stop for passengers of public mass transportation
or in the act of boarding
a bus or other public transportation vehicle;
or (3) In or near a school zone or a school crossing zone
marked in accordance with NRS 484B.363
or a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.

What the driver must exercise shows in the vehicle's conduct toward the observed pedestrian: its motion, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the duty read while it moves above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and the outcome caution exists to prevent, rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', which is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss'; the near miss is bounded by the operationalization of z2.

Observing is a perception; the ontology reads what was in an actual road user's line of sight as rel.visible, 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body' (observable_reading, perception). Its exclusions — a distance, the sight distance of a place, the clarity of the air, a lamp being lit — do not apply: the words name what the driver could see of an actual pedestrian.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate.

'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic'), 'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city') and 'road' (DEF-NRS-484A-215, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway outside the territorial limits of a city') are all highways, and together every highway whatever the city limits: st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway', and the words name the whole way. 'On' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; 'near' is st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)', at most p.pedestrian_near_reach. st.region_geometry is 'Not a stand-in for: occupancy', which is why rel.occupies carries 'on'.

'a bus stop or bench, shelter or transit stop for passengers of public mass transportation' is st.transit_stop, 'a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers'. 'Stop' here is part of the place name 'bus stop' and 'transit stop', not the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 or DEF-NRS-484A-260 defines. 'At' is rel.occupies of the stop's region and 'near' is its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, which also anchors the stop to the pedestrian.

Boarding is read through the conduct that shows it (observable_reading, purpose): the pedestrian within p.pedestrian_near_reach of the vehicle's body, rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', while the vehicle is at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt 'The road user is at rest at the observation', and has a door open, sig.door_open 'a door open'. The halt concept 'says nothing of how long the road user stays at rest, where it is, or why', which the reading does not need.

'Bus' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus ('a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision or a private school or nursery, designed for carrying more than 10 passengers ... or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation'), claimed as ru.aggregate. 'Other public transportation vehicle' is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported ... upon a highway', excluding devices 'used exclusively upon stationary rails') that is in public transit service: ru.transit_bus, 'bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display', a class the words name on their own and no definition admits.

'School zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-063, 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and 'school crossing zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-060, 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are administrative categories; the law takes them where they are 'marked', and the ontology makes the sign the atom where a category is marked on the road: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}', with kind school or school_crossing and its end attribute false; the sections of street are the travel regions it governs, dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', of kind st.travel_region. dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now', which the words do not ask: the zone, not its hours, places the pedestrian. 'In' is rel.occupies of such a region and 'near' its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach.

'marked in accordance with NRS 484B.363' is the zone's marking: dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing. Its accordance with NRS 484B.363, a statute outside this corpus, is the legal status of a feature, read through the sign's presence (observable_reading, status).

'Crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065, '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute', both values of the attribute read since the words name 'a marked or unmarked crosswalk'. 'In or near' (carried from z9) is rel.occupies of the crosswalk or its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach.

operationalizations.standard: proper caution upon observing a pedestrian (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, caution shows in its keeping no contact and no closest approach to the observed pedestrian, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, visible from the subject at that observation (rel.visible), and at one of the places: (1) p's footprint overlaps a highway (st.highway) or its ground distance to one (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach; (2) p's footprint overlaps a transit stop (st.transit_stop) or its ground distance to one is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, or p's rel.surface_gap to a road user v that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus, or a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that is an ru.transit_bus, is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach while v is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) and has a door open (sig.door_open); (3) p's footprint overlaps, or its ground distance is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach to, a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing that begins a zone, or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of caution, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'upon observing' is read as the pedestrian being in the subject's line of sight at the observation judged; a pedestrian seen earlier and occluded now is not read.
'in the act of boarding' is read through the conduct that shows it: the pedestrian close to a halted bus or transit vehicle with a door open.
the marking's accordance with NRS 484B.363 is read through the presence of the school or school-crossing zone sign.

Proper caution, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with the observed pedestrian; slowing, lookout and every other aspect of caution are read only through that outcome.

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
Between adjacent intersections
at which official traffic-control devices are in operation
pedestrians
shall not cross at any place
except in a marked crosswalk.

elements.justification: 'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', alley junctions excluded as the definition's (3) excludes them. 'Adjacent intersections' are two intersections with none between them along the way; the pedestrian is between them where its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) recorded as a directed approach to one of them, i1: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', the carrier being 'the stretch one direction of travel uses to reach one junction' — so nothing lies between c's stretch and i1 — and the other, i2 ≠ i1, is reached either through a second carrier the pedestrian also occupies that enters i2 (the opposing direction of a two-way way), or, where c is a lane (st.lane), through a lane that enters i2 and leads into c, directly or through one lane between (st.lane_connectivity, 'which lane a lane leads into'). The relation atoms tie both intersections to the pedestrian's own carriers; no distance stands for belonging. A pedestrian at either intersection is not between them: its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2, nor a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). st.lane_enters is 'Not a stand-in for: ... the region a device governs', which v3 reads separately.

'Official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'). The law's own words 'are in operation' qualify the devices and limit which members the duty reads: a device in operation is one that operates, displaying indications, so they leave out signs and markings, which are posted or painted but do not operate, and signal heads that are not operating — covered, dark, or inoperative. The members read are signal heads: dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {...}; uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered') with its uncovered attribute true and a state other than dark, and not dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'). The device is at the intersection where it governs it, dev.governs 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', or governs a carrier recorded as entering it (st.lane_enters), as the st.lane_enters contract directs: 'which intersection a device controls is read through both, or directly where the device governs the intersection'; dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position'. 'Official' is the device's legal status, read through its presence (observable_reading, status). Each of i1 and i2 must have such a device.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate as the index maps 'No pedestrian'.

To cross is to move across the way: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r', with r the carrier c the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), as the index maps 'crossing a roadway' for LVMC_11_30_060_A. The concept 'says nothing of whether a occupies r', which rel.occupies supplies; a pedestrian at rest or walking along the carrier is not crossing, as the concept excludes.

'a marked crosswalk' is st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute'), DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2) 'Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface'; 'in' it is rel.occupies of that crosswalk by the pedestrian, as the index maps 'except in a crosswalk'.

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; neither LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 nor LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 applies to it (ruleApplies, subject mapped to subject); and at the observation it is between adjacent controlled intersections: its footprint overlaps a travel region c (rel.occupies) recorded as entering an intersection i1 (st.lane_enters), and an intersection i2 other than i1 is found either because its footprint also overlaps a travel region recorded as entering i2, or because c is a lane and a lane that enters i2 leads into c (st.lane_connectivity) directly or through one lane between; each of i1 and i2 has a device in operation — a dev.traffic_signal that is uncovered, whose state is not dark and that is not dev.inoperative — that governs it (dev.governs) or governs a travel region recorded as entering it; and its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2 nor a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of); and it is moving across c (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, c) with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.crossing_motion_cos).
obligation: At that observation the subject's footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) whose marked attribute is true (rel.occupies). Otherwise violated; where the crosswalk's occupancy or its marking is unobserved, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'official' is the devices' legal status, read through the presence of the signal heads.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Mid-block between two intersections each governed by an operating traffic signal, a pedestrian walks across both directional carriers of the roadway, outside any crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Between the same two signalized intersections, a pedestrian walks across the roadway within a marked mid-block crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks across a roadway mid-block between two intersections controlled only by stop signs, with no signal head at either.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses mid-block outside any crosswalk between two intersections with signal heads; which regions the signal heads govern is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses at the unmarked crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of the approach into a signalized intersection: it is at the intersection, not between.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian who is not blind approaches a person carrying a white cane while crossing mid-block between two signalized intersections, so LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 applies to it.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
